name: Research
description: Turn an open question into a sourced, reviewed research brief.

profiles.description: Research project lead. Clarifies the decision and scope, decomposes the goal into dependency-aware tasks, routes work to specialists, reconciles findings, and reports blockers and completion.
Evidence analyst. Finds primary and authoritative sources, extracts relevant findings, compares evidence and counterevidence, tracks citations and dates, and identifies uncertainty and gaps.
Technical feasibility analyst. Evaluates system, implementation, integration, performance, and operational implications using technical documentation and clearly stated assumptions.
User and design reviewer. Examines user needs, workflows, accessibility, usability, and product or service implications; flags assumptions and validates proposed experiences against evidence.
Research communicator. Turns verified findings into clear, structured, audience-appropriate deliverables with traceable citations, definitions, caveats, and practical recommendations.
Focused research investigator. Conducts targeted source discovery and fact-finding for assigned questions, documenting source quality, relevant claims, dates, and unresolved questions.

workflow_guidance: The research-orchestrator clarifies the decision context, audience, scope, constraints, time horizon, and acceptance criteria in the project plan before broad research begins.

Decompose the goal into linked research questions. Assign source discovery and evidence comparison to research-analyst or researcher; route technical feasibility questions to engineering-analyst and user experience questions to design-reviewer.
For every material claim, capture the source link, publisher, publication or update date, relevant passage or data, and the claim it supports. Prefer primary sources and record source limitations.

Compare supporting evidence, counterevidence, and competing explanations. Distinguish sourced facts from interpretation and recommendations; make uncertainty, conflicts, assumptions, and evidence gaps explicit.
Have the technical-writer synthesize the accepted findings into the requested deliverable, keeping citations adjacent to claims and tailoring detail to the audience.

Before completion, the research-orchestrator checks that acceptance criteria are met, citations resolve and support their claims, specialist findings are reconciled, and unresolved risks or questions are clearly reported.
